description: An integration lead's doctor --delivery, lead-integrate and status line name each delivery registered on its integration target with what its queue is checking and has queued, and the supervisor journals target.settled once a target peer has merged and every target peer's queue has been empty for the window, 600 seconds unless lead-wait --target-quiet sets the record's own; with no integration target, or no delivery on it, nothing changes. lead-init and lead-run --resume end with the one live view the lead opens in the host's browser pane, unasked: the hosted view when hosted is enabled and has a URL, else the local live view's address, and nothing while no supervisor runs; delivery.orient names the same view to a lead, never to a lane. The commands that carry out an orchestrated delivery, layered on the delivery views: lens round briefs and round files, gate runs, in-app checks under a lease, draft change requests, lane hand-offs, and the lead's setup, assignment, acceptance, evidence, ship and close-out. A delivery whose stories declare criteria also gets the plan chapter's input, written by lead-side commands alone, with every change to the approved plan recorded. The plan's own review runs through plan-review commands with no round bound, kept in a durable store every plan write reads and fitted to the plan's caps; lead-setup drafts approvals and out of scope from the plan, and lead-plan approval marks one done. A binding may let the lead choose a candidate's checks from its diff, recorded per reviewed head and voided by a new head; the record, results, views and stats name the lead's choice and reason, and without the option the provider selects as before. A tracker with an adapter gets its updates and moves posted by the tracker publisher, which the binding runs on every render and which keeps its own ledger, so each is made once. Lanes begin a story with lane-start, which records the start the tracker's start move waits for; open-pr and pr-review make the review move when tracker.transitions.reviewWhen says, and handoff posts its own update. Two host hooks run through the generation's dispatcher, each switched off, warn or enforce in the configuration: lead.may-stop holds a lead's stop while a lane works or a candidate is queued and no lead-wait listens, journalling hook.held, and delivery.orient tells each session in a delivery its role and next command. Delivery records can hold lane ownership, current story assignments, and temporary flakes scoped to a base commit and check. Authorized base merges can retain an aligned review through hand-off. Integration-base setup records its target and uses the integration checkout for delivery. Record writers are pinned by applied archive digest and changed through a parked lead transition. Integration-base moves preserve recorded commit ancestry and recover publication and applied-writer reconciliation once. A stopped base rerun is told from a failed one, a named repair lands first and alone through a queue its broken base stopped, and a finish line that covers nothing is the lead's to mark. Follow-ups are filed only for findings still deferred, a round card says when an approval carried deferrable notes, and a delivery may declare that it defers nothing. A base move that changed nothing a check reads, by the binding's own declaration, carries that check, and deliveries that merge into one base on a machine share one merge slot. The line map labels a carried check, a flaky base run and a peer's merge. A failed full-health run whose failing tests pass alone is recorded as flaky where the binding declares the rerun, lead-suite runs the lead's suite in its own checkout of a commit, and deliveries on one base see each other and warn on files a peer claimed. A bounded data-only public snapshot reuses line-map payloads while excluding history and raw artifacts. Optional owned hosted publishing collects coherent source cuts, reconciles fenced writer receipts and keeps credentials out of view data and children. Owned hosted publishing starts or adopts an independent generation-aware watcher, bounds terminal close publication to 30 seconds, retains pending terminal cuts for ten-minute retries and supports credential-free archive viewing with explicit archive retry. Credential-free terminal notifications reach an existing owner independently of lifecycle-lock contention and preserve one deadline per finished cut. Hosted publishing is qualified from exact built archive bytes in two independently configured adopters; the separately deployed viewer and its dependencies are excluded from workflow archives. Any service that conforms to hosted-delivery-api/1 is a valid hosted origin: the Cloudflare Worker, the portable container built from the release's verified service bundle, or one's own implementation that passes the conformance suite. Hosted diagnostics report configured hosting before a delivery is selected without reading or creating delivery state; missing credentials and malformed configuration remain explicit. The hosted page shows what the local live view shows, from the same record; a cut holding a configured secret's value or a credential-named field is refused with its code, which the retried status names, and a sibling's hosted link, which grants read access to that delivery, is left out as a credential. Workflows may consult an optional, read-only knowledge library after the repository's own solution notes; the hive knowledge adapter maps it to the host's hive-mined server, configured by the repository's knowledge properties, and a workflow reports that the library was not consulted when none is configured. Journal entries hold typed facts by registered kind with their causes and no sentence; a record in the older journal shape is refused and closes under the release that wrote it. A narrator tells the journal as a story of chapters, beats and setbacks that open and close. The views show the delivery's story at three depths. The hosted snapshot moves to version 3 and refuses the earlier one. Run-delivery writes its entries as facts, the lead records a decision with its reason or a blocker by command, and the tracker posts the kind registry's words. A hand-off and the lead's acceptance can name a check whose catalogue entry the candidate's own committed binding adds, before the entry reaches the base; the hand-off marks it as added, and an id in neither catalogue is refused. A candidate that adds or removes provenance outputs syncs over a base that only refreshed digests, taking the candidate's listing and regenerating; when both sides changed the listing it stops as before. lead-authorize-base-merge also prints how to finish a merge that stops on a conflict, and a base merge's authorization trailer is read with comment lines dropped, so no git version or comment setting decides whether a review carries; a last merge that lost its trailer is refused with the exact amend that fixes it, and an earlier one is refused with word to merge again. A lane's aligned review carries across an authorized base merge when the story's own change reads the same before and after it, compared both ways hunk by hunk with an appended separator counted as a change, whoever owns the files the base touched; a round a base merge forces counts against the bound. A hand-off is refused when the head conflicts with the current base outside the regenerable paths, or conflicts in a regenerable listing that both sides changed, and names the files and the base-merge command; with base-merge a lane authorizes its own merge of the current base before hand-off, journalled as its own decision, and a merge that leaves the story's change unchanged keeps the aligned review. Once a check of a lone candidate's run has failed, a new hand-off supersedes the rest of that run and any base re-run that follows, on the lead's acceptance, or on the hand-off itself when the delivery needs no acceptance; a batch run is never superseded. The acceptance journals check.superseded, and the queue then stops the checks it started, writes no verdict and never checks the old head again; lead-base-broken names the base broken before a re-run's verdict, with --repair naming another candidate or --self-repair making the failing story's next accepted head the repair; without either, a failed check re-runs on the base as before, and the line map says what a running re-run is for, when it should end and what the lead can do instead. A story's review runs the mandated lenses plus the declared story lenses its lane chooses at round 1 with review-prepare --lenses and --lenses-reason, fixed for the story and shown at hand-off and acceptance; a lens declared for plan review only never reviews a story, and without a choice every declared story lens runs. A supervisor child that won't stay up, and a checkout an interrupted lead-suite left where the merge queue refuses to run beside it, are journalled as blockers the lead's wait hears, and the supervisor removes such a checkout itself once no run uses it. When a story lands, the region claims granted for it are released, and its lane's other claims on a file the merge changed are carried over the lines the landing changed inside them, or named in Needs you as needing a regrant; a claim that no longer maps doesn't block a grant on its file. lead-own --carve replaces a file's claims whole or changes nothing, a lane's touching claims for one story become one, claims-check lists every line a lane's diff still needs, and lead-claims previews the queue's ownership check. Each supervisor pass reads every assigned lane's pushed story branch from its merge base with the delivery base and writes lane-changes.json beside the record, reading an unchanged branch once; Needs you names each change to a file the lane doesn't hold, or to lines outside its span, without holding the close, a declared shared output raises nothing, and a branch that can't be read is named in place of the lane's items. lead-init writes the integration step for a delivery with an integrationTarget, lead-suite journals integration.suite there with a passed, over-budget, unreadable or failed result, and lead-integrate journals the target merged in, an integration review round, the change request into the target and its merge. Every region grant, carve and carry prints its spans' first and last lines at the base; lead-own --around TEXT names a span by the enclosing function, statement, Markdown section or indented block of the one line holding TEXT, refusing a missing or ambiguous anchor with its candidates; a Python span whose edge cuts a statement is refused; --insert before or after widens a span by one unclaimed line so an insertion at its edge falls inside it; and claims-check asks for spans by anchor. A close fast-forwards the operator's checkout when it is clean and on the delivery's base or its integration target, and otherwise names why it left it; lead-retire, which lead-close runs last, removes the lead's own checkout once the archive holds every journal entry, nothing of the delivery runs from it and it has no change and its head is pushed, and otherwise names what keeps it; and the lead ends or archives the lane sessions it started. A per-machine ledger, shared by every repository on the machine, records each heavy run's claim on a capacity of slots and its measured cost; heavy commands claim and wait by default when the machine is full, an agent steps off a default with a recorded reason, and the Machine view shows who is using the machine. A Node below the runtime's minimum first on PATH gives way to an nvm Node that meets it, which the tool puts first on its own PATH for itself and every process it starts. On macOS the supervisor keeps the machine awake while it runs, and it starts again by itself on a release applied while it runs, moving the record's writer pin to it. A lane's change to a file outside its claims is refused at review-prepare, review-reduce and handoff, naming the lead-own --grant, or --move for a file another lane holds, that clears it before review; lead-accept --take is for a file the lead narrowed out of the lane's claims after the lane handed off. A binding may declare regenerable.shared outputs, which a lane changes with no claim: the queue verifies a candidate's shared outputs on its own commit, in a temporary worktree, with the base binding's prepare, lead inputs, regenerators and postSync, before it merges the base in, and stops with shared_output_irreproducible or shared_output_generator_failed; a binding without shared behaves as before. review-prepare, review-reduce, handoff and lead-accept verify a change to an output the base binding declares under regenerable.shared in place of a claim, keeping a passing result by commit and base binding, and the lead reads what is shared from the base branch's head, never its working tree.
